meta.description: Calculates statistical power for high-dimensional genomics experiments (bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, methylation, proteomics) under negative-binomial count models using RNASeqPower, PROPER, and simulation via powsimR, distinguishing per-gene from marginal (transcriptome-wide) power, the role of mean expression and dispersion, and the sequencing-depth-versus-replicate tradeoff.

scientific_integrity.detail: All nine references checked (spot-verified independently in this audit: Hoenig & Heisey 2001, Am Stat 55:19, confirmed via publisher record; Liu 2014 Bioinformatics 30:301, Schurch 2016 RNA 22:839, Hart 2013 J Comput Biol 20:970, Wu 2015 PROPER Bioinformatics 31:233, and Vieth 2017 powsimR Bioinformatics 33:3486 were independently verified against their stated journal/volume/page during the prior audit of the closely-related sibling Skill experimental-design/sample-size, which cites the same works; Button 2013 Nat Rev Neurosci 14:365, Gelman & Carlin 2014 Perspect Psychol Sci 9:641, and Ioannidis 2005 PLoS Med 2:e124 are well-established, correctly formed citations). No fabricated DOI, PMID, sample size, p-value or efficacy figure found in the Skill or in any of the seven outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Nothing in the Skill or in any of the seven outputs diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual. The regulated clinical-trial regime is explicitly handed off to clinical-biostatistics/power-and-sample-size in both the frontmatter description and the decision tree, and Input 6 confirms an agent following the Skill actually takes that hand-off rather than improvising a regulated calculation.

methodological_ground.detail: The central methodology is sound and four of its non-obvious claims were independently confirmed in this audit: PROPER's delta parameter is genuinely natural-log (not log2) fold change, verified against PROPER's own source (makeMeanExpr.2grp uses exp(lBaselineExpr + lfc/2) so a 2x fold change is lfc=log(2)); closed-form and simulation power materially disagree at the same nominal parameters, exactly as the Skill's own Common Errors table predicts; replicates beat depth at equal sequencing spend (power 0.625 at depth-heavy vs 0.857 at replicate-heavy allocation); and population scRNA-seq power is set by donors, not cells (pseudobulk power ~0.000 at 4 donors regardless of cells/donor, vs cell-level testing at 0.87-0.89 realized FDR). The two real gaps found -- proteomics dropping proteome-wide multiplicity control, and the undocumented units of 'depth' -- are omissions, not fallacies, and are recorded as P1 recommendations rather than a redline.

code_usability.detail: Every code block the Skill actually ships was executed and ran without error and produced real, checked-against-independent-methods numeric output: the SKILL.md rnapower() closed-form block, the SKILL.md PROPER simulation block, and the shipped examples/rnaseq_power.R run verbatim end-to-end (exit 0, every printed number sane and internally consistent -- power rising with n, marginal power rising with Nreps, FDR gap closing with more replicates, depth-saturation curve correct). This is a clean contrast to the sibling Skill experimental-design/sample-size, whose flagship code block failed on 21/21 calls.

functional_suitability.note: Bulk RNA-seq (the Skill's central case) has complete, correct, runnable code for both the closed-form and simulation routes. But three of the five named assay types -- scRNA-seq, ATAC/ChIP/methylation, and proteomics -- exist only as a one-line taxonomy/decision-tree entry with no code anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md or examples/, so a researcher following those rows gets a principle, not a procedure.

reliability.note: rnapower() was swept across n=2 to near-impossible targets (1.01-fold effect, 95% power) and never returned NA, an error, or nonsense -- always a real, monotone, interpretable number, unlike the sibling Skill's ssizeRNA. The Category 2 fault-tolerance override applies favourably here since nothing silently produces a flawed protocol. One deduction: the Skill gives no interpretive text for when the computed n is not fundable (e.g. n=3276).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md stays under 180 lines with depth deferred to usage-guide.md and one example script; the decision tree routes an agent to the right approach in one lookup.

agent_usability.note: Per-Method Failure Modes table (trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix) is excellent and every entry checked out under test. Deductions: the 'depth' parameter's real-world units (how it maps to a stated sequencing budget in reads or millions of reads) are never defined, so Input 2 required the auditor to invent a scaling assumption; and the reviewer-pushback table promises a 'power curve provided' that no shipped code produces.

human_usability.note: Description and usage-guide Quick Start phrasing match how a researcher actually asks. Applying the Category 2 forgiveness override (strict numeric inputs are a scientific-integrity requirement, judged on whether required parameters are stated): required parameters are named but 'depth' is never given a concrete definition or worked conversion from a real read budget.

security.note: No credentials, no network calls, no eval/exec, no file writes, no PHI; every input is a numeric design parameter, so the injection surface is effectively nil. One point withheld for no documented parameter-range validation (e.g. alpha/power outside (0,1)).

maintainability.note: Clean three-file layout, one concern per section. The shipped example is genuinely testable: run verbatim it exits 0 and every line of output is a real, internally consistent number, confirmed by this audit -- a direct contrast to the sibling Skill's example, which prints NA and NaN as its headline answers.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision and composability are both very strong, with explicit hand-offs to five sibling Skills including the correct clinical-trial regime exclusion. Idempotency: no SKILL.md or examples/ block calls set.seed, but repeated runs of the identical PROPER block were measured to be byte-identical -- because PROPER's own RNAseq.SimOptions.2grp hard-codes a default sim.seed=11111 internally. This gives real determinism today, but it is an undocumented reliance on the underlying package's default rather than something the Skill manages itself.

key_strengths: The shipped example (examples/rnaseq_power.R) runs verbatim end-to-end with exit 0 and every printed number is real, sane and internally consistent -- a direct, checked contrast to the sibling Skill experimental-design/sample-size, whose example prints NA and NaN as its headline answers.

A genuinely subtle, easy-to-get-wrong detail -- that PROPER's delta parameter is a natural-log, not log2, fold change -- is stated correctly in the Skill and was independently verified against PROPER's own source code.

Three of the Skill's non-obvious quantitative claims were independently confirmed by simulation in this audit: replicates beat depth at equal sequencing spend, population scRNA-seq power is set by donor count not cell count, and observed/post-hoc power is a deterministic function of the p-value alone.
rnapower() was stress-tested from n=2 to a near-impossible 1.05-fold/95%-power target and never returned NA, an error, or a nonsense value -- it degrades gracefully across the whole practical range.
Escape hatches and scope boundaries are well designed and were confirmed behaviorally: the Skill correctly routes clinical-trial endpoint power to a named sibling Skill rather than attempting it.

recommendations.title: scRNA-seq, ATAC/ChIP/methylation and proteomics routes ship with no executable code
recommendations.problem: Three of the five assay types in the Algorithmic Taxonomy and Decision Tree exist only as prose. powsimR (the named scRNA-seq tool) is GitHub-only and not installed; no pseudobulk-sizing pattern, ATAC/ChIP NB-simulation pattern, or proteomics pwr.t.test block appears anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md or examples/.
recommendations.root_cause: Progressive disclosure stops at the bulk RNA-seq case; the other four assay types were documented conceptually but never given a worked code pattern.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal pwr::pwr.t.test block for proteomics (trivial, since pwr is already a stated dependency), a pseudobulk-on-donors DESeq2/edgeR pattern for scRNA-seq that needs no extra dependency, and either pin a powsimR commit with a documented install fallback or drop it from the primary recommendation.

recommendations.title: Proteomics route drops proteome-wide multiplicity control
recommendations.problem: The decision tree sends proteomics to pwr.t.test at alpha=0.05 per protein with no multiplicity step. Across a realistic 4000-protein panel, the prescribed n (12 at d=1.2) is 3-7x smaller than what proteome-wide FDR control requires (n=43 Bonferroni-equivalent), and the row gives no caveat.
recommendations.root_cause: The Gaussian per-protein route was added without carrying over the FDR-aware framing used everywhere else in the Skill (per-gene power, marginal power at target FDR).
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit alpha adjustment to the proteomics row (sig.level = 0.05/n_proteins, or a simulation-based BH step) and state the resulting n alongside the raw uncorrected figure so the two are never confused.

recommendations.title: rnapower()'s 'depth' parameter has no documented units or real-budget conversion
recommendations.problem: Every budget-tradeoff example (including the shipped script's own 'Depth vs Replicates' section) manipulates 'depth' without ever stating what unit it is in or how to derive it from a stated sequencing budget (e.g. 20 million reads per sample).
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill inherits RNASeqPower's own terse documentation ('average depth of coverage ... common values 5-20') without adding the conversion step a researcher actually needs.
recommendations.fix: Add one worked example converting a stated total-reads budget to RNASeqPower's depth units (e.g. via mapped reads / number of expressed genes / a normalization constant), and state the assumption explicitly.

recommendations.title: No guidance when the computed sample size is not fundable
recommendations.problem: rnapower() correctly returns a real but very large n for near-impossible targets (e.g. n=3276 for a 1.05-fold change at 95% power), but the Skill gives no instruction for what to do next -- report the achieved power at an affordable n, suggest a coarser effect size, or flag infeasibility explicitly.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill documents only the case where a reasonable n exists within a practical range.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'when the target is not fundable' note: report power at the affordable n, or solve for the minimum detectable effect at that n instead of an unreachable sample size.

recommendations.title: Simulation determinism rests entirely on an undocumented PROPER package default
recommendations.problem: No SKILL.md or examples/ block calls set.seed(); repeated runs of the identical PROPER block were measured to be byte-identical only because PROPER's own RNAseq.SimOptions.2grp hard-codes sim.seed=11111 as its default. The Skill neither documents nor relies on this explicitly.
recommendations.root_cause: Seed management was left entirely to the underlying package's own default rather than made an explicit part of the Skill's instructions.
recommendations.fix: State explicitly that RNAseq.SimOptions.2grp's default sim.seed=11111 is what makes the quickstart reproducible, and show how to pass a different explicit seed (sim.seed=) for a documented, intentional re-run rather than an accidental one.
